abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of machine learning approaches for binary network intrusion classification using the NSL-KDD dataset (63,280 training, 22,544 test samples, 121 features). Three algorithm families were investigated: Ensemble Methods (BaggingClassifier), Non-Linear Methods (DecisionTreeClassifier), and Support Vector Methods (RidgeClassifier). Results demonstrate clear performance stratification: BaggingClassifier achieved 91.60% balanced accuracy and 0.8244 MCC with 87.20% attack detection rate. DecisionTreeClassifier achieved comparable results (91.19% balanced accuracy, 0.8160 MCC) with interpretability advantages. RidgeClassifier substantially underperformed (79.18% balanced accuracy, 0.5894 MCC), with bias-variance decomposition confirming underfitting due to linear separability limitations. Key findings: non-linear methods are essential for intrusion detection, model family selection matters more than hyperparameter optimization, and ensemble methods provide marginal improvement over single trees for this dataset.
